forces.title: Decline in Food & Beverage Exports Due to Softened International Demand
forces.description: Irish food and beverage exports experienced a 3% decline in H1 2026 compared to 2025, reaching €9.1bn. This downturn affected several subsectors, including beverages, meat, dairy, seafood, and horticulture. The overall softening of international demand is a primary contributor, creating a more challenging trading environment for alcoholic beverage producers. This necessitates a strategic focus on diversifying export markets and product portfolios to mitigate geopolitical and trade-related risks and maintain competitiveness.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: High Input Costs and Weather Volatility Drive Margin Pressure
forces.description: Food and beverage producers across Europe, including those in the alcoholic beverages sector, continue to face severe margin pressure. Elevated energy and staffing costs, global market disruptions, and extreme weather affecting agricultural yields and production costs are major challenges. A 2026 report highlighted that 91% of food businesses reported increased costs in 2025, with 85% anticipating further rises in 2026. This indicates persistent profitability headwinds, requiring vigilant cost management and operational efficiencies.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Extreme Weather Impacts Raw Material Availability and Costs
forces.description: Western Europe experienced exceptionally high temperatures and very low rainfall in summer 2026. This weather volatility severely impacts harvests, affecting the availability and cost of raw materials crucial for food and drink production, including alcoholic beverages. Producers face increased production costs due to these conditions, contributing to overall margin pressure and posing a significant headwind for the sector. Strengthening supply chain resilience and investing in sustainable agricultural practices become critical to mitigate future weather-related risks.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Automation and Robotics Investments Enhance Efficiency and Offset Labor Shortages
forces.description: Food and beverage producers are increasingly investing in automation, robotics, and integrated production methods to improve productivity and manage costs. These initiatives also help to offset persistent labor shortages within the sector. By streamlining operations and upskilling employees for automated environments, businesses are building long-term resilience and competitiveness. This widespread adoption of advanced technologies represents a significant structural change, allowing alcoholic beverage producers to enhance operational efficiency and maintain profitability in a high-cost environment.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: New EU Packaging Regulation Increases Compliance Costs for Producers
forces.description: The EU Regulation 2025/40 on Packaging and Packaging Waste (PPWR), effective August 2026, introduces stringent requirements for recyclability, labelling, and reporting, alongside bans on certain packaging substances. Alcoholic beverage producers, like all EU food and drink companies, must assess and adapt their packaging across EU markets. This regulatory shift presents an initial headwind due to increased compliance costs and operational adjustments, but also drives sustainability initiatives, forcing investment in product development and process improvement for environmentally friendly packaging solutions.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: EU Deforestation Regulation Increases Supply Chain Traceability Needs
forces.description: The EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), effective December 2026, mandates that companies importing certain commodities into the EU prove they are deforestation-free and legally produced. For alcoholic beverage producers, particularly those using wood for barrels (e.g., whisky, wine), this regulation significantly increases supply chain traceability and compliance requirements. This structural change presents a headwind, demanding greater transparency and potentially higher costs for sourcing and verification, pushing companies to invest in robust supply chain management and certification systems.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Spirits Sector M&A Drives Portfolio Diversification and Market Presence
forces.description: Cobblestone Brands, an Irish spirits company, expanded its portfolio significantly through recent acquisitions. In 2026, it acquired Bisquit & Dubouché Cognac and Cabo Wabo Tequila from Campari, adding to its 2025 purchases of Knappogue Castle and Clontarf whiskeys. This M&A activity demonstrates a strategic focus on broadening presence across various spirits categories, including whiskey, rum, gin, cognac, and tequila. This consolidation trend allows companies to gain market share, diversify product offerings, and achieve economies of scale in a competitive environment.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Sustainability Investments Driven by Consumer and Regulatory Pressure
forces.description: Despite persistent cost management priorities, food and beverage producers across Europe, including those in alcoholic beverages, are increasing investments in sustainability initiatives. This is a direct response to growing emphasis from consumers, retailers, and regulators on environmental performance and ethical production. This trend represents a structural change in industry operations, as companies seek to align with evolving market expectations and comply with new regulatory frameworks, potentially leading to long-term competitive advantages and an improved ESG profile for the sector.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Increased R&D Tax Credits Boost Innovation and Competitiveness
forces.description: The increase in Ireland's R&D tax credit rate from 30% to 35% provides significant incentives for businesses across the food and beverage sector, including alcoholic beverages, to invest in innovation. This enhanced support encourages product development, process improvement, and technology adoption, which are critical for maintaining competitiveness and responding to evolving consumer demands. It acts as an upside driver, fostering long-term growth and differentiation in a challenging market environment by enabling companies to invest in future-proof solutions.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Rising Fuel and Transport Costs Squeeze Agrifood Margins
forces.description: Ireland's agrifood sector, which serves as a crucial supplier of raw materials to alcoholic beverage producers, faces tightening profitability in Q2 2026. Rising fuel prices and increased processing and transport costs, largely linked to the Middle East conflict, are weighing heavily on margins. This represents a significant headwind for the alcoholic beverages sector, as higher upstream costs for ingredients (e.g., grains, sugar) and logistics will inevitably translate into increased production expenses, challenging overall profitability and necessitating careful cost management.
forces.source_title: July 2026 Ireland Sector Snippets

forces.title: Geopolitical Conflict Escalates Energy and Input Costs for Agriculture
forces.description: The US/Israel war with Iran has directly caused upward movements in key agricultural input prices in 2026, specifically for agri-diesel and, consequently, fertiliser. While feed prices remained stable, the overall increase in energy costs for farming operations implies higher raw material expenses for alcoholic beverage producers relying on agricultural inputs like grains and fruits. Despite Irish government fuel support schemes, this geopolitical-driven cost inflation acts as a significant headwind, pressuring margins within the alcoholic beverages supply chain.
forces.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

forces.title: Growing Global Demand for High-Quality Greek Food and Beverages
forces.description: The Greek Food and Beverage industry, including alcoholic beverages, benefits from a rising global demand for high-quality products, those associated with the Mediterranean diet, and sustainable production practices. This trend creates significant export opportunities for Greek companies, reinforcing their position in international markets. This represents a tailwind, allowing producers to capitalize on their reputation for quality and differentiate their offerings in a competitive global landscape, thereby driving increased revenue from international sales and enhancing market penetration.
forces.source_title: Food and Beverages Industry. Facts & Figures 2025

forces.title: Digital Transformation Drives Innovation and Competitiveness
forces.description: The Greek food and beverage industry, encompassing alcoholic beverages, is undergoing a profound digital transformation. This involves leveraging technological advancements like automation, data analytics, and e-commerce across production, distribution, and R&D. Driven by evolving consumer habits and demands for quality, safety, and sustainability, companies are adopting new operational models. This represents a structural change, enhancing competitiveness and enabling growth strategies responsive to the digital age and increasing efficiency across the value chain, fostering long-term resilience and innovation.
forces.source_title: Food and Beverages Industry. Facts & Figures 2025

forces.title: Rising Cereal Prices Impact Production Costs for Alcoholic Beverages
forces.description: International cereal prices are rising in 2026, posing a direct headwind for alcoholic beverage producers, particularly brewers and distillers that rely on grains like barley, wheat, and maize as key raw materials. This commodity price increase contributes to elevated input costs, which, combined with other inflationary pressures, will squeeze profit margins. The volatile commodity market environment necessitates careful procurement strategies and potentially hedging arrangements for IN050105 companies to mitigate the impact of price fluctuations.
forces.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

forces.title: Increased Energy Costs for Agriculture and Processing
forces.description: Irish agriculture is forecast to experience a 20% increase in transport fuel expenditure and a 5% rise in electricity prices in 2026 compared to 2025. These elevated energy costs for primary producers translate into higher raw material costs for the alcoholic beverages sector. Furthermore, direct electricity costs for brewing, distilling, and bottling operations will also increase, presenting a significant headwind that will contribute to margin compression for IN050105 companies. This emphasizes the need for energy efficiency investments and strategic procurement.
forces.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

forces.title: Elevated Commodity Prices and Supply Chain Uncertainty Drive Food Inflation
forces.description: Food price increases are a major consumer focus in 2026, driven by a confluence of factors impacting the Irish and broader European grocery sector. Higher global commodity prices for wheat and sugar, increased overheads for retailers and suppliers (personnel, energy, insurance), rising farm-gate prices, and global trade uncertainty exacerbated by the Middle East conflict all contribute. For alcoholic beverage producers, these factors translate into higher input costs and supply chain risks, acting as a significant headwind on profitability and potentially impacting consumer demand due to elevated retail prices.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Retail Convenience H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Prolonged High Energy Costs Dampen Consumer Spending and Increase Production Costs
forces.description: A sustained inflationary environment, particularly driven by elevated oil and gas costs, poses a significant headwind for the retail sector, including alcoholic beverages. It directly increases business costs for energy, transport, and production within the IN050105 value chain. Concurrently, it reduces consumers' discretionary income and appetite for spending, especially on non-essential items. Retailers must adapt pricing and promotions without compromising brand positioning to navigate this challenging economic landscape, as prolonged high costs risk altering consumer behavior structurally.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Agricultural Input Costs Outpace Output Prices, Squeezing Farm Margins
forces.description: Agricultural input costs, including fertiliser, feed, and fuel, are rising faster than farm output prices, leading to significant margin compression and increased volatility across farm systems. This directly impacts the supply chain for alcoholic beverage producers, as higher costs for key raw materials like grains (for spirits and beer) and grapes (for wine) are a substantial headwind. IN050105 companies must absorb higher procurement expenses or pass them on to consumers, challenging their own profitability and requiring adaptive sourcing and pricing strategies.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Long-Term Geopolitical Conflict Threatens Global Grain Supply
forces.description: A prolonged Middle East conflict could significantly impact global agricultural markets, particularly by disrupting fertiliser supply and increasing costs. This may lead farmers to shift from energy-intensive crops like maize to less fertiliser-dependent alternatives such as soya. Such a shift would potentially reduce global grain supply in the long term (2027), leading to higher grain prices. This represents a key risk for alcoholic beverage producers reliant on grains for production, potentially driving up raw material costs and increasing supply chain volatility.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Slowing Global Economic Growth Softens Demand for Higher-Value Products
forces.description: Higher energy prices are anticipated to slow global economic growth, which could soften demand for higher-value food products. As alcoholic beverages often fall into discretionary spending categories, this trend presents a headwind for the IN050105 sector. Reduced consumer purchasing power may limit or reverse potential price increases that producers need to implement to offset rising input costs, challenging both sales volumes and profit margins for premium and standard products. This requires companies to adapt their value propositions.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Lower Alcohol Consumption and Weakened Consumer Spend Pressure Sector
forces.description: The alcoholic beverages sector is experiencing significant pressure from a trend of lower overall alcohol consumption and weakened consumer spending power in Ireland. This demographic shift towards reduced alcohol intake, coupled with economic factors impacting discretionary spending, directly affects sales volumes and profitability. This persistent headwind necessitates producers to adapt strategies, potentially focusing on premiumization, no/low alcohol alternatives, or value offerings to maintain market share and revenue in a contracting consumption environment, requiring innovative product development and marketing.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Diverging Beer Sales Trends: Retail Up, On-Trade Down
forces.description: The Greek beer market is experiencing divergent trends in its sub-markets. Retail sales of beer have strengthened in recent years, indicating sustained consumer demand in off-premise channels. Conversely, beer consumption in the on-trade market (HORECA) shows a downward trend, even with increased tourist flows. This presents a structural change, forcing brewers to adjust distribution strategies and focus on retail partnerships, while navigating reduced demand in hospitality despite tourism recovery. This impacts revenue mix and channel profitability, demanding flexible market approaches.
forces.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

forces.title: Doubling of Greek Beer Exports Strengthens International Position
forces.description: Greek beer exports reached €35 million in 2024, representing 10.6% of total production, and have doubled compared to the period before 2010. This strong growth signifies a strengthening international position for the Greek brewing industry. It acts as a tailwind, indicating successful market penetration and increased global demand for Greek beer brands. This provides a crucial avenue for growth and diversification away from potentially stagnant domestic consumption, supporting domestic producers through expanded international sales and improved brand recognition.
forces.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

forces.title: Growing Consumer Interest in Imported Beer Brands Increases Competition
forces.description: The value of beer imports into Greece reached €39 million in 2024, reflecting an upward trend and growing consumer interest in international brands. This increase in imported beer consumption presents a headwind for domestic brewers, intensifying market competition and potentially eroding market share. Producers must innovate and differentiate their products, perhaps through premium or craft offerings, to maintain relevance against a backdrop of diverse international offerings and evolving consumer preferences for variety, necessitating agile market strategies.
forces.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

forces.title: Increased Competition and Fragmentation in Greek Beer Market
forces.description: The Greek beer market has undergone significant structural changes, with Athenian Brewery's market share declining from 80% in 2000 to 54% in 2024. The emergence of Olympic Brewery (27% share post-merger) and other smaller players, including microbreweries, indicates increased competition and market fragmentation. This shift, reflected in a 43% drop in the HHI, means a more competitive landscape, challenging dominant players and creating opportunities for diversified product offerings and new entrants, requiring adaptation to evolving consumer preferences and market dynamics.
forces.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

forces.title: Consumer Shift Towards Local and Niche Beer Brands
forces.description: The Greek beer market is experiencing a notable shift in consumer preferences towards beer brands with Greek names and microbrewery products. This trend, coupled with the strengthening market share of non-alcoholic beer products, indicates a desire for local provenance and specialized offerings. Conversely, private label beers are seeing a decline in their share. This structural change demands that brewers innovate their product portfolios and marketing to align with evolving tastes and a growing appreciation for regional and craft options, fostering differentiation and new market entry.
forces.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

forces.title: Rising Production Costs and Taxation Drive Up Beer Prices
forces.description: Retail prices for beer products in Greece show a clear upward trend from 2014 to 2024. This increase is primarily a result of escalating production and distribution costs, along with successive increases in beer taxation. The rising cost base, amplified by higher excise duties (sixth highest in EU-27), acts as a significant headwind for the brewing industry. While contributing to state revenue, it risks impacting consumer affordability and potentially dampening demand, particularly in the price-sensitive on-trade market.
forces.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

forces.title: Reduced Profitability Due to Demand, Competition, Retailer Power, and Taxes
forces.description: The Greek brewing industry's net profit margin remains suppressed at 10.5% in 2024, a 4-5 percentage point drop from historical levels. This profitability decline is driven by a combination of factors: reduced demand for beer, intense price competition, the increasing bargaining power of large retailers, and higher excise duties. These cumulative pressures create a significant headwind for the sector, making it challenging to maintain healthy margins and necessitating strategic responses to cost and market dynamics to ensure long-term sustainability and competitiveness.
forces.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

forces.title: High Excise Duty on Beer Hampers Market Growth
forces.description: Greece's excise duty rate on beer is significantly high, having increased five times between 2009 and 2016 to nearly double the pre-2016 regime and five times the pre-2009 levels. It is the sixth highest in the EU-27, almost 50% above the EU average. This high taxation (42% of retail price) is a major headwind for the brewing industry, contributing to reduced demand, intense price competition, and suppressed profit margins, despite generating €203 million in state revenue in 2024.
forces.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

forces.title: Stagnant Beer Demand and On-Trade Spending Contraction
forces.description: The Greek beer market faces significant challenges from stagnant demand and curtailed consumer spending, particularly in the on-trade segment (HORECA). This headwind is exacerbated by the relatively small size of the domestic market and intense competition from other beverage categories. The combination of these factors limits growth potential, puts pressure on sales volumes, and necessitates innovative strategies for brewers to stimulate demand and maintain market relevance against diverse consumer choices, impacting overall profitability and market share.
forces.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

forces.title: Tourism Dependence and Seasonality Create Demand Volatility
forces.description: The Greek brewing industry is significantly affected by its dependence on tourism and the strong seasonality of demand. While tourism can boost sales during peak seasons, it also introduces volatility and makes the market susceptible to external shocks affecting travel and hospitality. This cyclical challenge, combined with intense competition and a relatively small domestic market, limits the sector's ability to achieve economies of scale and maintain stable demand throughout the year, posing a key risk for consistent profitability and strategic planning.
forces.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

forces.title: Climate Change Risks Raw Material Availability and Costs
forces.description: Breweries face escalating pressure from rising production costs, particularly due to more expensive raw materials like malt, hops, and energy, alongside increased transport costs. Furthermore, climate change is identified as a potential structural problem, threatening the cost and availability of these essential raw materials. This key risk implies long-term supply chain vulnerabilities and sustained inflationary pressures, compelling the alcoholic beverages sector to invest in adaptation strategies and potentially diversify sourcing to mitigate future impacts, ensuring continuity of production.
forces.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

forces.title: GLP-1 Weight-Loss Drugs Threaten Alcoholic Beverage Demand
forces.description: The growing adoption of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, currently used by at least 2% of adults in Europe and the UK (9-10 million users), poses a significant key risk to the alcoholic beverages sector. Studies suggest that GLP-1 users reduce calorie intake by 15-20%, with alcoholic beverages identified as one of the categories most exposed to declining expenditure and intake. This trend, especially if adoption accelerates and becomes more sustainable, could lead to a gradual but material reduction in demand for IN050105 products, impacting sales volumes.
forces.source_title: Transformative or overhyped? The impact of weight-loss drugs on European food…

forces.title: GLP-1 Impact Drives Redesigned Marketing Strategies for Beverages
forces.description: The increasing use of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs necessitates a strategic overhaul of marketing for alcoholic beverage companies. Faced with potentially reduced consumption among users, firms will need to refocus marketing efforts on consumers who are not using GLP-1s, who still represent the majority. Additionally, strategies to re-engage consumers who discontinue GLP-1 use will be crucial. This represents a structural change in marketing, requiring nuanced targeting and messaging to adapt to fragmented consumption patterns and ensure continued market relevance.
forces.source_title: Transformative or overhyped? The impact of weight-loss drugs on European food…

forces.title: Historical Tax Hikes and Recession Caused Significant Market Contraction
forces.description: The Greek spirits sector suffered severe market contraction due to a dramatic decline in income (2008-2013) and sharp increases in excise duty and VAT rates after 2009. Legal sales volume plummeted from 8.0 million 9-litre cases in 2009 to a low of 3.1 million in 2020, recovering only to 5.1 million in 2024 (64% of 2009 levels). This historical headwind led to an estimated 25,000 job losses, a €717 million GDP decline, and €136 million less labor income, creating a challenging legacy of reduced market size and profitability for the sector.
forces.source_title: The Spirits Sector in Greece: Contribution to the economy and prospects

forces.title: Increasing Spirits Exports Signal Growing International Demand
forces.description: Greek spirits exports saw an 8.5% increase in 2024, reaching €115 million, while imports declined by 10.4% to €198 million. This growth in exports, with an extroversion index of 67% (exports to domestic production), indicates strengthening international demand for Greek spirits, such as Ouzo. This acts as a tailwind, supporting domestic production and offsetting some of the challenges faced in the local market, driving increased revenue from international sales and enhancing the sector's global footprint and brand recognition.
forces.source_title: The Spirits Sector in Greece: Contribution to the economy and prospects

forces.title: High Spirits Prices Due to Taxation Impede Consumer Affordability
forces.description: Successive increases in excise duty and VAT rates caused spirits prices in Greece to rise by 35.1% from 2009 to 2024. In real terms, Greek spirits prices are the fourth highest in the EU, making them significantly less affordable relative to disposable income. This high price point, exacerbated by a 55.1% total tax burden on the final price, acts as a headwind, potentially dampening legal consumption and driving consumers towards illicit alternatives, thus challenging market growth and tax revenue collection, and impacting industry profitability.
forces.source_title: The Spirits Sector in Greece: Contribution to the economy and prospects

forces.title: High Unrecorded Alcohol Consumption Due to Tax Disparities
forces.description: Greece faces a significant key risk from unrecorded alcohol consumption, ranking fifth in the EU with a rate of 11.8%, and showing an upward trend since 2008. This is exacerbated by tax disparities, particularly between bottled tsipouro and traditional two-day distillates, which are taxed at approximately 29% of the official rate. The low tax regime and lack of controls incentivize illegal production and marketing, leading to substantial tax revenue losses (estimated €47.7 million) and undermining the legal spirits market and its sustainability.
forces.source_title: The Spirits Sector in Greece: Contribution to the economy and prospects

forces.title: Excise Duty Reduction to Combat Illegal Trade and Boost Legal Market
forces.description: Adjusting Greece's spirits excise duty to the European average (€1,930 from €2,548) is anticipated to significantly reduce illegal trade and shift unrecorded consumption to legal channels. This policy aims to create a controlled and secure market, generating additional tax revenues and fostering a robust business environment for the spirits industry. This represents a powerful upside driver, improving market integrity, boosting domestic production, and enhancing the sustainability and competitiveness of legal businesses in the medium term, with positive results for the entire Greek economy.
forces.source_title: The Spirits Sector in Greece: Contribution to the economy and prospects

forces.title: Global Spirits Market Diversifies Product and Geographic Focus
forces.description: The global spirits market remains highly competitive, prompting distilleries to diversify their product ranges through innovative blending, Ready-to-Drink (RTD) offerings, and new packaging formats like pouches. To reduce dependence on the U.S. market, Irish operators are actively shifting attention to growth opportunities in regions like Canada, India, and Mexico. This dual strategy of product innovation and geographic market diversification represents a structural change and an upside driver, aiming to enhance resilience and unlock new revenue streams in a competitive environment, ensuring long-term growth.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Food and Drink Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: Growing Demand for Low & Zero Alcohol Beverages
forces.description: The market for low and zero-alcohol beverages is experiencing significant growth in Ireland, with 15.3% of households purchasing these products in the four weeks to December 28, 2025, up from 9% the previous year. This trend represents a structural change in consumer preferences, driven by health and wellness considerations. It is a tailwind for alcoholic beverage producers who adapt by offering a diversified portfolio of no/low alcohol alternatives, but a headwind for those focused solely on traditional alcoholic products, necessitating innovation to capture this evolving market segment.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Food and Drink Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: ECJ Ruling Restricts 'Non-Alcoholic' Spirit Labels, Impacts Marketing
forces.description: A European Court of Justice (ECJ) ruling in November 2025 prohibited non-alcoholic drinks from being labelled as 'gin,' establishing a precedent for other spirit categories. This regulatory clarification significantly impacts future marketing strategies for alcoholic beverage producers venturing into the no/low alcohol space. While aiming for consumer clarity, it represents a structural change, requiring companies to revise product naming conventions and branding for non-alcoholic alternatives to avoid legal and reputational risks, ensuring compliance across EU markets.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Food and Drink Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: Elevated Food Inflation Drives Beer Price Increases
forces.description: Food inflation is expected to remain elevated in early 2026, leading to continued high costs that impact consumer prices. Specifically, beer prices are set to increase, with major players like Diageo and Heineken signalling price hikes for February 2026. This cyclical headwind, driven by persistent input cost pressures despite some commodity price easing, will likely affect consumer demand and sales volumes within the alcoholic beverages sector, as higher retail prices may deter price-sensitive consumers, necessitating strategic adjustments to pricing and promotional activities.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Food and Drink Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

viewpoints.title: Irish Beverage Exports Decline Amid Softening International Demand
viewpoints.description: Irish food and beverage exports declined by a modest 3% in H1 2026 compared to the previous year, with beverages specifically noted among the subsectors experiencing a downturn. This performance reflects a softening in international demand, creating a more challenging trading environment for exporters. Despite an exceptionally strong 2025, the sector now faces headwinds from reduced global appetite, necessitating careful market diversification to mitigate risks associated with reliance on specific export destinations.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

viewpoints.title: Specialized Beverage Stores and Bars Show Resilience in Challenging Retail Climate
viewpoints.description: While Ireland's overall retail sector faces declining sales volumes and a challenging trading environment, specialized stores for Food, Beverages & Tobacco, along with Bars, are demonstrating stronger performance. This indicates a segment-specific resilience within retail, suggesting that consumers continue to frequent these outlets despite broader cost-of-living pressures. For the alcoholic beverages sector, this trend offers a cautious positive outlook, implying sustained demand in key distribution channels like specialized retail and on-premise consumption, even as general consumer spending remains uneven.

viewpoints.title: Greek Food and Beverage Sector Resilient Despite Cost Pressures and Inflation
viewpoints.description: The Greek Food and Beverage industry, including alcoholic beverages, is navigating significant challenges such as rising energy costs, international inflationary pressures, and intense foreign competition. Despite these headwinds, the sector maintains strong growth prospects, demonstrating resilience. This positive outlook is underpinned by the high quality of Greek products, robust export momentum, and a consumer shift towards healthier food options, which could also influence demand for premium or sustainably produced alcoholic beverages. Strategic adaptation to digital transformation is also seen as a key growth driver.
viewpoints.source_title: Food and Beverages Industry. Facts & Figures 2025

viewpoints.title: Greek Brewing Industry Rebounds in Production with Growing Microbreweries
viewpoints.description: The Greek brewing industry has shown a positive rebound in recent years, with beer production reaching 4.31 million hectoliters in 2024, recovering from declines in the 2010s. This growth is bolstered by an increasing number of operating units, particularly new microbreweries established since 2010, which foster product diversification. The sector has strengthened its economic presence, overcoming various crises and contributing significantly to employment. This indicates a positive trajectory for production volumes and overall industry vitality.
viewpoints.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

viewpoints.title: Greek Brewing Industry Profitability Remains Subdued Below Historical Levels
viewpoints.description: The Greek brewing industry's net profit margin, at 10.5% in 2024, shows only partial recovery and remains 4-5 percentage points below its historical 14-15% levels. This persistent margin compression is attributed to reduced beer demand, intense price competition, the increased bargaining power of large retailers, and high taxation. Despite growth opportunities from microbreweries and innovation, the sector faces ongoing challenges in fully restoring profitability, suggesting a cautious negative outlook for financial performance in the near to medium term.
viewpoints.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

viewpoints.title: Greek Brewing Poised for Growth Through Microbreweries, Quality, and Innovation
viewpoints.description: Despite significant ongoing challenges, the Greek brewing sector has a strong foundation for dynamic growth in the coming years. This positive outlook is driven by the rise of microbreweries, increasing emphasis on quality and product differentiation, leveraging links with tourism and local products, and strategic investments in innovation and sustainability. Through targeted strategies, increased export-orientation, and fostering a more mature consumption culture, the industry is expected to enhance its economic contribution, strengthen local production, and build a more resilient and competitive future.
viewpoints.source_title: The Brewing industry in Greece: Trends, contribution to the economy and challenges

viewpoints.title: Alcoholic Beverages Sector Faces Multiple Pressures Including Lower Consumption
viewpoints.description: The alcoholic beverages sub-sector in Ireland is confronting significant pressures beyond general food and drink challenges. These include reduced fish quotas (which are less directly relevant but mentioned in context), tariffs, and notably, a discernible trend of lower overall alcohol consumption combined with weakened consumer spending. This confluence of factors, exacerbated by high input costs and supply chain disruptions from global conflicts, creates a challenging environment. The sector faces a cautious outlook, requiring strategic adaptations to navigate declining volumes and reduced discretionary spending effectively.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: Greek Spirits Sector Faces Persistent Challenges Despite Recent Recovery
viewpoints.description: Despite a recent recovery driven by increased tourist flows and stronger domestic consumption, the Greek spirits sector remains significantly affected by the post-2009 economic recession and adverse tax policies. A dramatic decline in income (2008-2013) and sharp increases in excise duty and VAT rates led to a substantial sales volume drop, resulting in 25,000 job losses and significant economic contraction. With 2024 sales still at 64% of 2009 levels, the sector faces ongoing challenges from high taxation and market contraction, signaling a cautious negative outlook.
viewpoints.source_title: The Spirits Sector in Greece: Contribution to the economy and prospects

viewpoints.title: Reduced Spirits Excise Duty to Significantly Boost Greek Economy
viewpoints.description: The IOBE estimates that reducing Greece's spirits excise duty to the EU average (€1,930 from €2,548) would substantially benefit both the Greek economy and the spirits sector. This policy is projected to strengthen entrepreneurship by integrating consumption into legal channels, streamline the tax framework, and decrease retail prices by 13.6%. Crucially, it is expected to increase GDP by €180 million and employment by 13,100 jobs while maintaining a balanced budget, signaling a highly positive outlook for this proposed policy intervention.
viewpoints.source_title: The Spirits Sector in Greece: Contribution to the economy and prospects
